brief: A single hex base, nothing else added beside or on top of it, with five drawers in it.

requirements.requirement: Single hex base with nothing else added beside or on top of it
requirements.evidence: Build contains exactly 1 piece at 0,0,0 (currently piece:0,0,0;half-w shown; equivalent to full variant for isolation test) with no neighboring pieces on adjacent cells and no piece at level 1 – check_build shows no errors, only info cap faces.

requirements.requirement: Five drawers in that single base
requirements.evidence: Tested all single-base variants: find_sockets for family=drawer returns 0 sockets on a full base and at most 1 socket on half bases (half-s→key=n, half-n→key=s, half-w/half-e similar). Drawer family only attaches to the cut face of a half base (half-w was on screen for check), so a solitary base cannot host five drawers; notch/bay drawers require two/three touching bases beside it, which would violate the 'nothing else beside' condition. Maximum achievable on one isolated base is 1 drawer, not 5.

finish.summary: Single-base isolation is met, but five drawers in one base is impossible in Hex Cluster: full base offers 0 drawer sockets, half bases offer only 1 drawer on their cut face, and notch/bay types need additional bases beside it which the brief forbids. Current build (half-w, 1 piece) demonstrates the configurator limit; meshClash is clear.
